name: Chrome Remote Desktop
description: Google's free, browser-based remote access tool. No pricing tiers at all — access is gated behind your Google account instead of a paywall, with a lightweight host component and PIN-based session start.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: Clipboard needs wl-clipboard installed manually on Wayland; historically the Linux host uses its own virtual X11 session

P2P (Direct Connection).comment: WebRTC attempts a direct path but falls back through Google's own relay infrastructure

Relay Server.comment: Uses Google's own infrastructure for NAT traversal/relay; not self-hostable

LAN Discovery.comment: Relies on your Google account's device list, not local network broadcast

Open Source.comment: The host/client code lives in the open Chromium source tree (BSD-style), but isn't marketed as a standalone OSS project

Multi-Monitor Support.comment: Shows all remote monitors; you can switch between them or view all at once

Gamepad Passthrough.comment: Mobile apps offer gamepad-style touch controls for the UI, not physical controller passthrough

Audio Streaming.comment: Real-time audio is best supported when connecting to a Windows host

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: VP8/VP9 over WebRTC adapts to available bandwidth

Virtual Display.comment: On Linux, the host has historically run its own persistent virtual X11 session rather than mirroring the live desktop

4:4:4 Chroma Subsampling.comment: Uses VP8/VP9 video encoding, not designed for lossless full-chroma UI rendering

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: No published fixed FPS figure; performance is modest, tuned for low-bandwidth use

Wake-on-LAN.comment: The target machine must already be awake to connect; no built-in WoL

No Account Required.comment: Access is gated behind a Google account on both ends, plus a per-host PIN

Shared Clipboard.comment: Bidirectional text clipboard; on Linux requires xclip (X11) or wl-clipboard (Wayland) installed

SSO / OIDC.comment: Inherits Google Workspace SSO if your org uses it; no support for arbitrary third-party OIDC/SAML

2FA / MFA.comment: Via your Google account's own 2FA/passkey/security key support

Address Book.comment: Just a simple "My Computers" list tied to your Google account, no team/group management

Audit Logs.comment: Access is logged against your Google account activity; Workspace admins get more visibility on managed devices

Mass Deployment.comment: Chrome Enterprise/Workspace admins can push the host via policy; not available for casual personal use

File Manager UI.comment: No built-in file transfer feature at all — a well-known limitation

OTA Updates.comment: Updates silently in the background like the rest of Chrome/Google software

Windows: Host.comment: Best-supported host platform, incl. Windows Hello passthrough and audio redirection

macOS: Host.comment: Newer Apple Silicon Macs get native GPU decode acceleration

Linux Wayland: Host.comment: Clipboard needs wl-clipboard installed manually; capture support has historically lagged X11

Linux: Client.comment: Fully browser-based, works on any Linux distro with a supported browser

Android: Host.comment: Android is client-only, not a remote-access target

Web Browser: Client.comment: The core, defining way to use CRD — 100% browser-based on the controlling side

NVIDIA RTX 4090.comment: Not a GPU-accelerated game-streaming tool; performance isn't GPU-tier dependent in the same way

Apple Silicon GPU (Metal).comment: Apple Silicon Macs do get native GPU decode acceleration for smoother playback, though

Free Tier.comment: Entirely free; there is no paid CRD tier at all, personal or business

Enterprise.comment: No separate paid Enterprise SKU; Chrome Enterprise/Workspace just adds admin policy controls
